one_line: Solanki king Kumarapala and Jain acharya Hemachandra, shaping 12th‑century Gujarat’s politics and ethics.

appearance.age_look: Kumarapala looks late 40s with a sturdy royal build; Hemachandra looks late 30s to early 40s with a lean scholar’s frame.
appearance.face: Kumarapala has an oval face, warm wheat-brown complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache, short close beard along the jaw, and steady, serious eyes with a calm but alert expression; Hemachandra has a slightly longer face, lighter brown complexion, fine straight nose, thin lips, no facial hair, soft but thoughtful eyes that narrow when he concentrates, and a gentle, composed smile that hints at quiet resolve.
appearance.hair: Kumarapala’s hair is black, cut short and neat under a red-and-gold conical royal turban (paghadi) with a central gold kalgi ornament and a narrow white cloth band; Hemachandra’s black hair is mostly concealed under a simple off-white cloth wrapped close to the head like a modest Jain monk’s hood, with only a thin, short fringe visible at the forehead.
appearance.costume: Kumarapala wears a mid-12th-century western Indian royal outfit: a knee-length, long-sleeved angarakha-style tunic of rich deep maroon silk with subtle gold woven buti dots, side-tied with a thin gold cord; over it a sleeveless, slightly shorter golden-yellow brocade vest with narrow red edging; a pleated white cotton dhoti wrapped tightly to the ankles with a broad maroon border, forming neat front pleats; a long cream shawl with maroon and gold stripes draped from his left shoulder across the torso and looping behind; jewellery includes a medium-width gold necklace with a single round pendant, a pair of simple gold karnaphool earrings, and two gold bangles on each wrist; on his feet are brown leather mojari-style shoes with slightly upturned toes and minimal embroidery in maroon; Hemachandra wears a modest, fully draped Jain monk’s ensemble in keeping with regional textiles: an unpatterned off-white cotton upper garment like a long-sleeved, calf-length robe that overlaps in front, tied with a plain cloth belt, and a separate off-white lower wrap tightly covering from waist to the ankles; over his shoulders he has a light beige cotton shawl with a very narrow brown border, wrapped so it covers his chest and falls evenly; his clothing is clean but unadorned, with no jewellery, emphasizing simplicity; both are always fully and modestly clothed.
appearance.signature: Kumarapala’s signature prop is a sheathed straight-edged steel sword with a simple slightly-curved crossguard and a brown leather-wrapped hilt, hanging from a maroon cloth-and-leather belt at his left hip; Hemachandra’s signature prop is a neatly rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle bound with a thin red cord that he often holds in his left hand.

ref_desc: Kumarapala is a wheat-brown, bearded king in a deep maroon angarakha, golden-yellow vest, white dhoti, cream striped shawl, red-and-gold turban and sheathed sword, standing beside the lean, clean-shaven Hemachandra in simple off-white Jain robes with a beige shawl and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript, all in maroon, gold, off-white, cream and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two fixed characters from 12th-century Gujarat: on the left, King Kumarapala, a sturdy late-40s man with a wheat-brown complexion, oval face, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache and short jawline beard, serious eyes and a calm, alert expression; his black hair is short under a red-and-gold conical turban with a central gold ornament and a narrow white band. He wears a knee-length deep maroon silk angarakha with subtle gold dots, a slightly shorter sleeveless golden-yellow brocade vest, a tightly wrapped white dhoti with a maroon border, and a long cream shawl with maroon and gold stripes draped from his left shoulder across his torso. He has a medium-width gold necklace with a single round pendant, simple gold earrings, two gold bangles per wrist, and brown leather mojari shoes with slight maroon embroidery. At his left hip hangs a straight-edged steel sword in a plain scabbard, with a simple crossguard and brown leather-wrapped hilt on a maroon cloth-and-leather belt. On the right, Hemachandra, a lean late-30s to early-40s man with a slightly longer face, lighter brown complexion, straight nose, no facial hair, thoughtful eyes and a gentle, composed smile, stands modestly; his black hair is mostly hidden under a simple off-white cloth hood. He wears fully covering, unadorned off-white cotton Jain robes: a long-sleeved calf-length upper garment overlapping in front, tied with a plain belt, a matching lower wrap to the ankles, and a light beige shawl with a thin brown border draped to cover his chest and shoulders. He is barefoot and carries a neatly rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord in his left hand. Keep the colour palette centered on deep maroon, golden yellow, off-white, cream and brown, and show them from multiple angles to emphasize their consistent face shapes, hair, garments and signature sword and manuscript props.
